chapter_title: Concerning the Fifty Lord's Days; to what Mysterie

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
Know that within each external truth by which the Divine first works in the outermost degree there dwells a sufficient set of interior faculties. These faculties are brought into order in relation to one another until their sufficiency is completed in fullness.

When directed influx descended into a lower degree, the receptive answering within what received it at the same time yearned to rise toward its source. Directed influx together with compliant reception brought forth a full series of determinate spiritual qualities in a full series of distinct forms of action; these are the derivative powers proceeding from the Divine in its engagement with what stands in the way. Through these derivative powers, directed influx and compliant reception were lifted into higher states, because these powers supplied the ordered forms by which elevation could be effected.

As the Divine good that first enters combat with opposition raised itself by means of these ordered operative forms, so by those same forms everything in higher and lower degrees was set in order and held together. This is the complete cycle of a full spiritual process, the archetypal pattern of all states made holy in regeneration. In that cycle they abstained from what is merely their own, refusing to take their life from selfhood.

From then onward, until the coming of Divine truth in revealed glory, the nourishment of their inner life was the living provision of the soul: directed influx joined with compliant reception. Through the whole fullness of that complete cycle they were sustained by it, because that living nourishment was sufficient for all of them. It filled them with operative strength, with abundance, and with spiritual vitality; and by it the understanding was illumined and all within them was enriched.

paragraph_translations.translation: Know that within each external truth through which the Divine good first operates in the outermost degree there is a sufficient set of interior faculties. These are brought into mutual order, one with another, until that sufficiency is completed in its full measure. When directed influx descended into a lower degree, the answering reception within the recipient at the same time desired to rise with it toward its source. Directed influx together with compliant reception constituted a full complex of determinate qualities in a full complex of distinct forms of operation; these are the derivative powers proceeding from the Divine good in its activity. Through these, directed influx and compliant reception were lifted into higher states.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS the inner structure of external truths into ordered powers and explains how descent and ascent occur together.
paragraph_translations.notes: The text’s phrase about “sons of the Man” is rendered as derivative powers proceeding from the Divine good; the personal language does not add distinct function beyond this.

paragraph_translations.translation: As the Divine good that engages directly with resistance elevated itself by means of these ordered operative forms, so by those same forms all things in higher and lower degrees were established and set in order. This is the complete cycle of a full spiritual process, the archetypal pattern of all states made holy. In that state they abstained from what is merely their own, refusing to draw life from selfhood.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS from ascent-by-forms into the ordering of the whole spiritual structure and names the process as a holy cycle.
paragraph_translations.notes: The designation of the cycle as “fifty great days” is taken as fullness of process; no additional distinct spiritual content is carried by the calendrical phrasing.

paragraph_translations.translation: From that state onward, until the coming of Divine truth in revealed glory, their nourishment was the living provision of the soul: directed influx united with compliant reception as spiritual food. Through the whole fullness of that complete cycle they were sustained by it, because that living nourishment was sufficient for all. It filled them with operative power, abundance, and life, and by it the understanding was illumined and all within them was enriched.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONTINUES by showing the ongoing sustenance and enrichment that comes from that same living influx-and-reception.
paragraph_translations.notes: The name “Jesus the Splendour” is translated functionally as Divine truth in revealed glory; the line about being “released from all these fifty days” is treated as being sustained through the whole completed process, but the verb sequence in the source is difficult and slightly uncertain.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single spiritual teaching: exterior truths contain ordered interior faculties; descent of directed influx evokes an answering ascent; together they generate a complete set of operative forms that allow elevation and universal ordering. It remains one voice throughout, with minor strain where the source’s calendrical and narrative phrasing compresses several ideas into unclear verb transitions.

findings.diagnosis: Largely clean correspondential substrate: the teaching proceeds by functional relations (summons/answer; descent/ascent; ordered powers/limbs) and generates the spiritual sense without needing jurisdictional administration. Minor stress comes from a numeric systematization (fivefold → 25) that could be an internal mnemonic rather than an overlay.
findings.evidence: Text: “in each one of these five garments… there are five powers… five times [is] their number… summons… answer… summons with the obedience [constitute] twenty-five characteristics in their twenty-five limbs… sons of the Man.” This is functional/process language: descent (“summons went down”), responsive ascent (“answer wished to ascend with it”), and emergent forms (“characteristics… limbs”) that act as means of raising. The spiritual reading did not stumble here; it said the personal phrase “sons of the Man” “does not add distinct function beyond this,” indicating the narrative still works by function even with mythic naming.

findings.diagnosis: Clean continuation of the same correspondential process, with a small seam where a calendrical identification is appended (“pentecost, the fifty great days”). This looks like a liturgical/glossary-style naming of the process rather than an administrative jurisdiction list; it does not introduce ranked authorities or territorial governance, but it does momentarily switch from functional description to cultic label.
findings.evidence: Text: “raised himself up through them… by these… have set up all things above and below” (functional, causal means). Then: “Indeed, these are what are called pentecost, the fifty great days that are the archetypes of the holy days.” The spiritual reading explicitly noted strain: “The designation… as ‘fifty great days’ is taken as fullness of process; no additional distinct spiritual content is carried by the calendrical phrasing.” That is the hallmark of a naming gloss at a seam: it labels what was just taught rather than advancing it by function.

findings.diagnosis: Insertion/expansion at a seam: the narrative shifts from an atemporal functional cycle into a dated salvation-historical timeline (“from that time until… the advent of Jesus the Splendour”) and contains a garbled verb transition about “released from all these fifty days.” This is characteristic of Mani-layer systematizing: attaching the cosmic process to a christological identifier and to a historical interval, which the correspondential teaching does not require to function.
findings.evidence: Text: “from that time until… the advent of Jesus the Splendour” introduces a historical anchor and named figure; the spiritual reading admitted it had to convert the name functionally (“Jesus the Splendour… Divine truth in revealed glory”)—a classic sign the proper name is not participating in the functional mechanics of the teaching. Further, it noted: “the line about being ‘released from all these fifty days’… the verb sequence… is difficult and slightly uncertain,” matching the Coptic’s evident compression/garbling: “They rele[ased from] all these fifty days… this living food suffices…” The chapter’s functional story (living food = summons/obedience sustains) flows better without the salvation-historical frame and the broken ‘release’ clause.
findings.scope:
Excise the seam-expansion phrases that impose a salvation-historical frame and contain the garbled transition:

1) “So, from that time until [the time] of [the advent]ent of Jesus the Splendour,”

2) “They rele[ased from] all these fifty days,”

findings.diagnosis: No administrative overlay block is present: there are no ranked lists of authorities, jurisdictions, camps, watches, or stations. Even the numeration (5, 25, 50) is embedded in functional process (powers/limbs/days-as-archetypes) rather than governance.
findings.evidence: Across the chapter the driving verbs are processual and instrumental (“summons went down… answer wished to ascend… were raised… set up all things… living food… suffices… filled… illumined”). The spiritual reading was able to keep a single narrative, only flagging minor strain at the calendrical label and a difficult verb sequence—consistent with a mostly intact substrate with a small seam expansion.

textual_criticism.summary: 4 findings: (1) ¶2 is clean correspondential teaching (no action). (2) ¶3 contains a brief calendrical naming seam but not an administrative overlay (no action). (3) ¶4 shows a seam-expansion with christological/historical anchoring and a garbled transition; recommended excision of two short phrases. (4) Overall confirms absence of administrative block; chapter is predominantly correspondential with one likely Mani-layer seam.

changes_summary: Applied Finding 3 (¶4) excisions: removed the salvation-historical seam phrase “So, from that time until [the time] of [the advent]ent of Jesus the Splendour,” and removed the garbled transition “They rele[ased from] all these fifty days,” per the critic’s scope.
